recipes.name: Unbelievable Squash Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
0.5 (6 ounce) box dry bread stuffing mix

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a baking dish.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook and stir squash and onion until tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Add water and simmer to soften squash, 2 to 4 minutes.
Stir cream of chicken soup, sour cream, and Cheddar cheese into squash mixture; mix well.
Transfer squash mixture to the prepared baking dish; top with stuffing mix.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is bubbling and stuffing is browned, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Unbelievable Squash Casserole
raw_recipe.description: A creamy squash casserole topped with stuffing is the perfect dish for potlucks, weeknights, or any night of the week.

review.reviewBody: A delicious dish that I modified slightly. As I steamed cooked my squash, I made a mixture of the other ingredients by omitting the cheese and adding shredded fresh carrots and sweet, succulent pimentos. I put a cup of the cornbread stuffing on the bottom of my 9x13 dish, added my squash mixture and then put another cup of the cornbread stuffing on top. Baked in the oven at 350 degrees F for 30 minutes. Whoooooooo, Buddy! Boy howdy, did this turn out great! My cat and I highly recommend that you use the cornbread stuffing over any other type of stuffing. I think I need to hit up my brother for some more fresh squash so I can make it again.

I have one very much like this one, 1 pkg. of Pepperidge Farm herb stuffing, and use 1 lb. zucchini and 1 1/2 lbs. summer squash....cook the cubed squash & onions in boiling water with salt. drain, fold it into the soup & sour cream, (which has been mixed together. Mix the bread crumbs with melted butter, then layer half bread crumbs on bottom of 9 x 12 pan, then the squash mixture, then top with the rest of bread crumb mixture....I will try the cheese next time I make this, it is delicious....also think in summer to top it off with some fresh tomatoes under the cheese...YUM!!!!

Awesome! I doubled this for Easter takeaways. I added 1 1/2 cups shredded carrots to the onions and squash while sautéing. I used the big can of cream of chicken soup and added a whole chicken stuffing mix. I did not put cheese on top. I made a Ritz cracker crumb topping mixed with 1/2 cup of stuffing mix. This was really good.

Holy smoke. I am in no way a master chef. I read the reviews for this particularly easy bake and made a few modifications. First of all, I did add about half of the stuffing mix into the squash after cooking. The rest of the recipe I followed to a "t", with the exception of: I minced two cloves of garlic and cooked it with the onions and squash; instead of simmering in water, I simmered in Zickles juice, and I added some crushed red pepper to the oil before initially cooking the squash...only because I like a little spice. I did add the optional cheese because, well...cheese. This. Turned. Out. Amazing. Thanks for the base recipe! I'll definitely make and modify over and over and over!

My wife loves squash. This is similar to hotdish from my youth, without the ground beef. I shredded the cheese with the coarse blade of my food processor and set it aside. Then the summer squash (4 cups). Shredding the squash second makes cleaning the disk easier. I fried the onion first, because the shredded squash cooks quickly. I suspect most kids would think the shredded squash was pasta.

I *always* read the reviews before I make a recipe. In this case I ended up shredding the squash in the food processor, and adding the (cornbread) stuffing mix to the squash mixture. I then topped it with the shredded cheese and some bread crumbs,since I put all the stuffing mix in the casserole itself. It was fabulous! My husband just ate his second squash casserole meal of the day!

The flavor is really good but please note: the squash needs to be longer in the pan and with more water ( I used Vegetable stock) to make sure it is soft before you assemble the caserole and add salt and lots of pepper...yummmmy.

I've been making this recipe for 40+ years, but with a few variations. I use Pepperidge Farms Herb stuffing mix (small bag or 1/2 large bag) and lightly coat the stuffing with melted butter. 

Steam or boil squash an onion until almost tender. (Drain if boiled) and mix squash with soup, sour cream, cheddar cheese, and shredded carrots.

Cover 9 x 13 pan with half or more of the coated stuffing mix; then the squash mixture; and top with remaining stuffing. Cook as this recipe directs, until it's bubbly and veggies are cooked. You may want to cover the top with foil to avoid it browning too much, and remove the foil the last 15 minutes or so to brown up.

I gave added cooked poultry to it on occasion but usually service it as a side with poultry. I also serve it with cranberry sauce.

I've been making this for years for Thanksgiving. I boil my squash with onions and salt and pepper until it is tender, but not falling apart. I omit the cheese and put in chopped water chestnuts, as well as the cream of chicken soup and sour cream. I put Pepperidge Farm herb dressing on the bottom and top. My family loves it and looks forward to it.

This is one of my favorite ways to use the mountains of summer squash from the garden. I just saute the squash and onion in butter until tender and skip the water. I only use about 1/4 - 1/2 cup of the sour cream and skip the cheese. Although I do not make a habit of using canned cream soups or packaged stuffing mix I will cheat for this recipe! Delicious. Note: I have tasted this before using low sodium products and did not like it nearly as well.

Delicious! The only modification I made was to salt & pepper the squash while it was cooking. I also keep my stuffing mix in a canister (there are only 2 of us and a whole box is too much to make at one time), so I just sprinkled it on top until it was the consistency I wanted, not sure how much it was, but know the whole box would've probably been too much. I've made this a few times and even our pickiest friend who doesn't like squash or onions went back for seconds. Thanks for sharing!I

Update: I make this all the time now and have made a couple more modifications. I sprinkle the stuffing mix on the bottom and sprinkle the top with French fried onions. So good!
One of my favorite casseroles. I enjoy it warm or cold. I cook my squash and onion in chicken broth but don’t add anything else.

This was phenomenal! I used 4 squash, 4 zucchini, 1 large yellow onion. Didn't need to add water. It took at least 15 minutes to saute and steam all those veggies, stirring every few minutes, covered. When they were tender I poured it into a colander to drain all the liquid. Then put it back in the pan, made a well, and added about 3 Tablespoons chopped garlic, and about 1 teas salt and 1 teas black pepper, and cooked a couple minutes. I used a 12 oz bag of herbed stuffing mix. I melted 1 and 1/2 sticks of butter and mixed that into the stuffing mix. I stirred in half of the stuffing into the squash mixture, then put it in a 9x13" glass pan (greased). Then poured the rest of the stuffing on top. Baked per recipe. Sooo good! Thank you!

Good comfort side dish. Cut a zucchini into 1" cubes and had about 8 cups. Didn't need to add any water and actually took off 2cups of liquid (based on other reviews). I added 2 tsp of salt to the squash when cooking with onions. Used ritz crackers and some Italian seasoning and pepper for the top. Nice way to use up more zucchini.

My mom always makes this no cheese with shredded carrots . I did it the way she does it with herb stuffing and kicked it up a notch. Never any leftovers cant stop eating it. This will always remind me of mom, so good. Love you Mom thank you for showing me how to cook and I showed everyone how to eat.
Its good and its simple to make. I halved the recipe using two small squash and it worked out well.
Added fresh onion and garlic and seasoned with McCormick Grill Masters Smokehouse Maple. Poured melted butter over stuffing topping before cooking.
delicious just as is.
added extra cheese and was a bit hit
I used crushed crackers instead of breadcrumbs. I also put in some zucchini. Was so delicious, will definitely remake.
